title: Kernel of a degreewise epimorphism is quasi-isomorphic to the shifted cone
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian] and let $f:P\to Q$ be a morphism of cochain complexes of $\mathcal A$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] such that $f^p:P^p\to Q^p$ is an epimorphism for every $p\in\mathbf Z$. Let $K\subseteq P$ be the termwise kernel, $K^p=\ker f^p$ with the restricted differential, and $\iota:K\to P$ the inclusion. With the mapping cone $\operatorname{Cone}(f)^r=Q^r\oplus P^{r+1}$, differential $(y,x)\mapsto(d_Qy+f(x),-d_Px)$, and the shift of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the complex $\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]$ has terms $Q^{p-1}\oplus P^p$ and differential $(y,x)\mapsto(-d_Qy-f(x),\,d_Px)$. Then the maps $\kappa^p=(0,\iota^p):K^p\to Q^{p-1}\oplus P^p$ form a morphism of complexes $\kappa:K\to\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]$, and $\kappa$ is a quasi-isomorphism; in particular $K\cong\operatorname{Cone}(f)[-1]$ in $D(\mathcal A)$.
